We need to read the problem carefully: Given a directed functional graph (each node points to exactly one receiver[i]), we consider walks of length k (k edges traversed) starting from a chosen node x. The function f(x) = sum of ids visited, including the starting node (i.e., we sum node id x + id after first pass + after second pass + ... + after k passes). Equivalent to sum of node ids along the walk of length k steps (so total k+1 nodes: start and then each pass yields a node). Actually description: f(x) = x + receiver[x] + receiver[receiver[x]] + ... + receiver^(k)[x]. The exponent notation: receiver^(k)[x] means apply receiver k times. So we have k+1 terms? Wait: The sum includes x (0 passes) + receiver[x] (1 pass) + receiver[receiver[x]] (2 passes) + ... + receiver^(k)[x] (k passes). So there are k+1 terms. The total sum includes k+1 nodes (if we consider after each pass). So f(x) = sum_{t=0}^{k} node_t, where node_0 = x, node_{t+1} = receiver[node_t] for t=0..k-1.

Goal: choose x to minimize f(x). Return minimal f(x) value (not the x). Constraints: n up to 1e5, k up to 1e10 (very large). So we need O(n log k) solution.

Observation: Since each node has out-degree exactly 1, each functional graph consists of cycles with trees feeding into them (in-arborescences). Starting from any node, after some steps you eventually reach a cycle and then continue moving around the cycle repeatedly.

For large k, after we enter the cycle, we will loop around many times. So we need to compute sum of nodes visited along the path (including the prefix before cycle) plus many full cycles plus a remainder.

Thus we need to compute, for each node x, the sum of ids visited over first k+1 steps. Since k may be large, we need to use binary lifting or doubling technique to compute k-step walk and sum of node ids along the path.
